#6157. The Two Card Answer To Which Rewards Strategy Is Actually Best

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

When I talk to people about earning miles, it’s inescapable that the majority of miles are earned from rewards credit cards. Most people want to know simply, “what is the best credit card.” If pressed I do have an answer to that question, but the best answer is that it’s usually two different credit cards that you pair together, taking the best of each.

The first thing to understand about rewards cards is that, in addition to their basic features as a payments tool, bundled financing, and consumer protections, there are really three different ways a card adds value. You need to understand this to make sure you’re using yours in the right way.

Initial bonus. A card might offer 100,000 points as an acquisition bonus. That’s a great reason to get a card, but it isn’t a good reason to keep the card or to spend money on the card (once you’ve earned the bonus).

Benefits. You might get free checked bags or priority boarding, lounge access, for free Disney+. Those can be great reasons to have the card, and keep the card, but aren’t reasons to spend money on the card (outside of the spend on those activities, potentially).

Rebate on spend. The most rewarding card for the kind of spending you’re doing – that means earning the most points, and the most valuable points, that you can redeem for the rewards you value most. When people ask about the best card, they’re usually talking about the one that gives them the best return on their spending. Although if they value a card’s benefits, they need to be careful to keep that issue separate – get that card, sure, enjoy the benefits, but don’t just default to using it for spending, too. I think that the American Express Platinum Card® (see rates and fees) is great to have, it is incredibly valuable for its benefits, but my goodness do not actually spend money on that card outside of airline tickets. For spending the reason you want two cards is that you generally want (1) that earns the most points in the categories you spend the most, and (2) a card that earns more than one point per dollar on everything else. Don’t fall into the trap of getting a ‘grocery card’ and then earning just one point per dollar on everything else. You can frequently get two cards where the second one has no annual fee, even. Here are some of the very best pairings: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (See rates and fees) has an offer to earn 100k bonus points after you spend $8,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. What’s great is earning 3x (on the first $150,000 spent in combined purchases) on travel, shipping purchases, internet, cable and phone services, advertising purchases made with social media sites and search engines each account anniversary year. It has the same points transfer partners as Chase Sapphire Reserve® (See rates and fees). And if you have some of the no annaul fee Chase cards, you can move the points from those cards over to Ink Business Preferred and then transfer them to airlines and hotel programs. And there are a number of Chase cards with no annual fee that earn points quickly, but on their own those points can’t be transferred to airlines or hotels. But if you earn points with one of those, you can transfer the points to your Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card and from there to miles and points in other programs. For instance, the Ink Business Cash card earns 5x on the first $25,000 in combined purchases at office stores and on internet, cable and phone services each account anniversary year. It earns 2x on the first $25,000 spent in combined purchases at gas stations and restaurants each account anniversary year. Freedom Flex earns 3X on dining and at drugstores and 5x in rotating categories, on up to $1,500 spend each quarter. The Freedom Unlimited card earns 1.5x on all spend (but 3x on dining and at drugstores). I have multiple Freedom and Ink Business cards, personally. Citi Strata Premier® Card (See rates and fees.) has a $95 annual fee. It earns 3x on groceries, dining, gas stations and on EV charging as well as flights and hotels. That’s really strong. It’s offering 60,000 bonus ThankYou® Points after spending $4,000 in the first 3 months of account opening. And the points even transfer to American Airlines AAdvantage miles. oneworld: American Airlines AAdvantage, Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, Qantas Frequent Flyer, Qatar Airways Privilege Club Star Alliance: Avianca LifeMiles, EVA Air Infinity MileageLands, Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer, Thai Airways Royal Orchid Plus, Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles SkyTeam: Air France KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club Non-alliance: Emirates Skywards, Etihad Guest, JetBlue TrueBlue Hotels: Leading Hotels of the World Leaders Club, Accor ALL – Accor Live Limitless, Choice Hotels Choice Privileges, Preferred Hotels I Prefer, Wyndham Hotels Wyndham Rewards There’s also a $100 Annual Hotel Benefit. Once per calendar year, you receive $100 off a single hotel stay of $500 or more (excluding taxes and fees) when booked through CitiTravel.com, applied instantly at time of booking. You can supplement that strong earner with a Citi Double Cash card which earns 2x on everything and has no annual fee. If you were going to get just one card for your spending, set it and forget it, and didn’t want to juggle products then I think the single best heavy spending card has to be the Bilt Palladium Card (See rates and fees). It’s a $495 annual fee card. It earns the most points on most spending, and it earns the most valuable points. The only thing to flag is that there are some things, like tax payments, that it doesn’t earn points for. So if you’re relying on big quarterly tax deposits for your points-earning this isn’t the card for you. You can earn 50,000 Bilt Points after spending $4,000 on everyday purchases in the first 90 days + $300 of Bilt Cash. The card earns 2X points on everyday spend. Plus, you can use Bilt Cash to earn 3x on up to $25,000 in purchases, you get a $200 twice annual hotel credit (with a 2-night minimum stay), and earning the card’s 50,000 point bonus after $4,000 in non-housing spend in the first 3 months also gives you Gold status for a year and that lets you earn Bilt points through Rakutent at 1:1. You can earn 3.3 points per dollar when spending 75% of the amount of your rent or mortgage and then using Bilt Cash to earn points when paying through through Bilt, and then earn 3 points per dollar redeeming Bilt Cash for points accelerator. So the cap on earning 3 points or more is much higher than that. There’s actually a strategy to earn 4 points per dollar on all of your spending by foregoing Bilt Cash entirely. You can spend points at 1.25 cents apiece directly through their travel portal, and they have the best transfer partners (and biggest transfer bonuses). Star Alliance: Air Canada Aeroplan, Turkish Miles & Smiles, United Airlines MileagePlus, Avianca LifeMiles, TAP Air Portugal Miles&Go oneworld: Cathay Pacific Asia Miles, Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan, Iberia Plus, British Airways Club, Japan Airlines Mileage Bank, Qatar Airways Privilege Club SkyTeam: Air France KLM Flying Blue, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club Non-alliance: Emirates Skywards, Southwest Airlines, Aer Lingus Aer Club Hotels: World Of Hyatt, IHG One Rewards, Marriott Bonvoy, Hilton Honors, Accor ALL – Accor Live Limitless, Wyndham Rewards Still, I’m going to add 4x and 5x cards to my wallet. But the Bilt Palladium Card is also a great option as your ‘catch all card’ paired with the card that earns the biggest multiplier on your primary spend. If you were going to get just one card for your spending, set it and forget it, and didn’t want to juggle products then I think the single best heavy spending card has to be the Bilt Palladium Card (See rates and fees).

It’s a $495 annual fee card. It earns the most points on most spending, and it earns the most valuable points. The only thing to flag is that there are some things, like tax payments, that it doesn’t earn points for. You can earn 3.3 points per dollar when spending 75% of the amount of your rent or mortgage and then using Bilt Cash to earn points when paying through through Bilt, and then earn 3 points per dollar redeeming Bilt Cash for points accelerator.

So the cap on earning 3 points or more is much higher than that. There’s actually a strategy to earn 4 points per dollar on all of your spending by foregoing Bilt Cash entirely.

You can spend points at 1.25 cents apiece directly through their travel portal, and they have the best transfer partners (and biggest transfer bonuses).

As soon as you apply for a credit card, your application is processed by a computer. You’ll typically receive one of three responses: immediate approval, some form of “pending” status or denial.

Receiving instant approval doesn’t guarantee that you can begin using your card immediately. If you receive instant approval, you may be able to view your card number right away; otherwise, you’ll usually need to wait until your physical card arrives in the mail before you can begin using it.

It can take five to 10 business days to get a new credit card after approval. However, that timeframe varies by card and issuer. For instance, American Express offers overnight shipping for its top-tier cards. Some issuers offer expedited shipping on request, but there’s no guarantee. You may need to pay when requesting expedited shipping from some banks (including Barclays).

The Points Guy believes that credit cards can transform lives, helping you leverage everyday spending for cash back or travel experiences that might otherwise be out of reach. We publish editorial content and card reviews to help you find a great card to turn your goals into reality.

Getting approved for a new credit card is exciting, but waiting a week or more for it to arrive in the mail isn't. Fortunately, some issuers let you start using your new card immediately after approval, either by providing an instant card number or by allowing you to add your card to a digital wallet.

That instant access can give you a head start on meeting the welcome bonus spending requirement, since the clock starts ticking as soon as your account is approved — not when your physical card arrives. It can also come in handy if you need to make a purchase right away, whether you're booking travel or taking advantage of a 0% introductory APR offer. For cobranded store credit cards, you may also receive a discount on your purchases, starting as soon as you use the card.

Here's a look at which major credit card issuers offer instant card numbers, digital wallet access or both.

Some issuers provide an instant card number, while others, like Chase, instead let eligible cardholders add their new card to a digital wallet immediately after approval. Both options let you start using your card before the physical version arrives.

While there are too many cards to list that offer instant card numbers or access, here are six of our top picks.

American Express provides your new account number immediately after your online application is approved, provided your identity can be verified.

The instant card number will be the same as the physical card you’ll get in the mail, but the four-digit card identification number on the front of the card will be different. Because of that, you may want to wait to set up recurring payments.

Note that instant card numbers for some cobranded cards may only be used with the cobranded company (like Delta, Hilton or Marriott).

In addition to instant numbers for new cardmembers, Amex gives existing cardmembers access to their card information when ordering replacement cards.

Most Amex personal and business cards offer instant card numbers; notable exclusions include the Amazon Business Card and the Amazon Business Prime Card.

The information for the Amazon Business and Amazon Business Prime cards have been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Occasionally, those with Bank of America checking accounts may receive a targeted promotion offering an instant card number for cards like the ; however, this is not standard practice.

You may be able to receive an instant card number by applying through the Bank of America app, but data points on this vary. Unless you already have an established relationship with Bank of America, you should plan on waiting for a physical card to arrive before use.

Related: The best Bank of America credit cards

With Barclays, you may be eligible to receive a virtual card number upon approval. When added to a digital wallet, this number can be used to make purchases until your physical card arrives.

You should be able to retrieve your virtual card number on the same page where you check your application status, provided you're approved for the card.

Capital One Mobile app users may be able to use instant card numbers immediately after they’re approved, before their physical card arrives in the mail.

This differs from Capital One's virtual card numbers, which are designed to help protect your purchases rather than provide immediate access to a newly approved account.

Some of our top picks for Capital One cards offering instant card numbers to eligible applicants are:

Related: Capital One Venture X vs Venture Rewards

Cardless focuses on cobranded credit cards you can use without a physical card. These are available instantly upon approval and can be used throughout the life of the card.

Through the Cardless app, you can access these cobranded cards and even get a new card number immediately if your card is ever compromised.

Cardless provides cobranded credit cards for brands like Avianca, Bilt and LATAM Airlines.

It is possible to use popular Chase cards instantly upon account approval by adding them to a digital wallet via Spend Instantly. These include the , (see rates and fees) and (see rates and fees).

It's important to note that this does not include a way to access an instant card number, but a way to instantly add your card to a digital wallet.

Here are the steps to set up Spend Instantly.

However, the issuer notes that several cards cannot be used immediately, including Mastercards, Amazon cards and business cards.

Citi offers instant card numbers for select cards if your application is approved instantly and your identity is verified. If eligible, you'll see a "Get Card Number Today" option after approval, followed by "See Card Summary" to view your temporary card number and security code. You’ll have just one opportunity to view this number, so be sure to write it down.

The (see rates and fees) works differently: Eligible applicants may receive a temporary barcode that can be used only for Costco purchases.

Availability varies by card and instant credit card numbers are not available on small-business or American Airlines credit cards, according to a Citi spokesperson. Some readers have also reported not having the option to get an instant card number with cards like the (see rates and fees).

Discover often gives you an instant decision on whether you’ve been approved for a credit card. After this decision, if eligible, you can receive a virtual card number to use online or add to a digital wallet.

The Discover it® Cash Back is our top pick. It is a good card for beginners and has rotating 5% quarterly cash-back categories.

SoFi's credit cards offer instant digital access, with physical cards arriving in the mail within 10 business days. These cards include:

The first two options offer great cash back. The SoFi Unlimited offers unlimited 2% cash back on all purchases. Meanwhile, the SoFi Everyday offers up to 3% bonus cash back in a variety of categories, including dining and groceries.

The information for the SoFi Unlimited 2% Credit Card, SoFi Everyday Cash Rewards Credit Card and SoFi Essential Credit Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Related: The best 2% cash-back credit cards

There are two Synchrony cards you can use immediately upon approval. However, you’ll only be able to use them instantly within digital wallets or within their respective apps: PayPal (for the PayPal Cashback Mastercard®) and Venmo (for the Venmo Credit Card).

You’ll need to wait for your card to arrive by mail before you can make purchases through other methods.

The information for the PayPal Mastercard and Venmo Credit Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

U.S. Bank typically offers instant card numbers only to consumer cardholders who have verified identities and a banking history with the bank. U.S. Bank has some excellent cash-back card offerings, including:

The information for the U.S. Bank Altitude Go and U.S. Bank Altitude Connect Visa Signature Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Wells Fargo generally does not offer instant card numbers, but you may be able to add your card to a digital wallet. Where you can use this virtual card may be restricted until your physical card arrives.

Some issuers offer expedited shipping for your new card. In most cases, though, you’ll have to wait roughly a week for your new card to arrive in the mail. Having instant access to your new card details can make a meaningful difference when you're working toward a valuable welcome bonus or need to make a purchase right away.

#6155. American Kept Charging A $75 Award Fee After No More Work Was Was Required, Former Loyalty Chief Says

American Airlines used to charge $75 to book an award ticket within 21 days of departure. Now the former head of AAdvantage says the airline kept collecting its expedite fee even after the process it was supposed to expedite became automated. Maya Leibman, who ran AAdvantage before becoming American’s Chief Information Officer, discussed this on the this week’s Airlines Confidential podcast. The airline finally eliminated the fee in January 2020. Leibman was defending checked bag fees because there are people and equipment involved in moving bags. Then she offered an example of a fee she couldn’t defend. I think she’s wrong about bag fees based on cost of production (‘real cost fallacy’). Bags are charged as a form of price discrimination. Nonetheless, Leibman recalled the transition from a manual award process to online booking: “we were still charging an expedite fee, like, within 21 days.”

Maya Leibman, who ran AAdvantage before becoming American’s Chief Information Officer, discussed this on the this week’s Airlines Confidential podcast. The airline finally eliminated the fee in January 2020.

Leibman was defending checked bag fees because there are people and equipment involved in moving bags. Then she offered an example of a fee she couldn’t defend. I think she’s wrong about bag fees based on cost of production (‘real cost fallacy’). Bags are charged as a form of price discrimination. Nonetheless, Leibman recalled the transition from a manual award process to online booking:

“we were still charging an expedite fee, like, within 21 days.”

The transaction, she pointed out, was “all done automatically.” The fee survived even though the narrative used to justify it was gone. The $75 close-in charge was waived for American’s elite frequent flyers.

American once tried to go further. In May 2008 they announced a $5 charge for booking award tickets on their website. The argument for telephone booking fees had been that agents cost money, and customers could avoid that charge by doing the work themselves online. Here American wanted to charge for the cheaper booking channel, too. I wrote about the announcement on May 30, 2008. Multiply millions of award redemptions by $5 and it was clearly a revenue opportunity since they were the monopoly redeemer of the currency. Members couldn’t take their AAdvantage miles and book travel somewhere else. Except the airline had already used the prospect of an award to persuade customers to earn those miles. Adding a charge when they tried to use them reduced the value of a reward they’d earned, and made it less likely they’d earn in the future. It left a bad taste in the customer’s mouth at exactly the moment they’re supposed to feel best about giving the airline business. As I wrote years ago, American never implemented that fee. They backed away without announcing the reversal. They took the criticism for imposing it and didn’t claim credit for listening to members. The Airline Had Already Been Paid To Give You Those Miles I don’t think airline prices have to track the cost of each transaction. Two passengers on the same flight, in the same cabin, pay different fares every day. Airlines price based on demand. There’s even an economic argument for charging more for last-minute awards: the airline might otherwise sell that seat for an expensive ticket, or the customer might otherwise pay cash for that expensive ticket. In the former case, revenue management is supposed to price the award so that’s not an issue. And neither case requires someone to hurry up and process an electronic ticket. Ultimately, eliminating a cash fee doesn’t even necessarily mean make awards cheaper. When American dropped its $75 charge, I pointed out that United and Delta had moved towards collecting more miles for close-in awards instead. That’s a bad trade for elites who used to have the cash fee waived but don’t get the extra mileage requirement waived. American stopped discounting awards to elites. I confess that there are times when I have, academically, mused about someone just walking behind the proverbial desk and changing a ticket (or something) in response to a fee.

Obviously there are all sorts of legal issues with that sort of thing, but the legal pleading would be amusing to read. “Blah Airlines charges a fee for a staff member to change a ticket. We are therefore suing John Doe for changing his own ticket. Because that’s bad.”

That was such an egregious fee because 1) it was fake, 2) they would release award availability close in, so then you had to pay the fee if you wanted access to the seats. Unless we have another recession, it is only a matter of time before they bring it back unless you have their stupid credit card.

Modern American Capitalism sucks. Time to burn it down with a new American Revolution, and a government that put consumers and workers first.

A former UFC champion was recording an interview in the lobby of the Hilton Abu Dhabi Yas Island when another fighter walked up, slapped him across the face, and set off a group brawl that left the man bloodied. Abu Dhabi police have since announced 10 arrests: eight people over the fight, and two more for filming it. They were guests traveling with the combatants but they were filming it seems rather than fighting. On Wednesday, November 11, Merab Dvalishvili was doing promotional work for Saturday’s Real American Freestyle wrestling event when Usman Nurmagomedov and several companions approached him Dvalishvili turns toward Nurmagomedov, who speaks to him and then slaps him. Then the melee spreads through the lobby. 🚨 Full footage of the scuffle between Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili https://t.co/SGJzkQdFif — Red Corner MMA (@RedCorner_MMA) November 11, 2026 Dvalishvili and wrestler Saba Lazishvili were left visibly injured. Dvalishvili says they were ambushed by a group he described as roughly 20 people, and that the beating continued while security restrained him. Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me – They kept kicking us when we were down like losers. The two men weren’t even scheduled to face each other. Dvalishvili was suppposed to wrestle Marlon Moraes at Etihad Arena on November 14. Usman wasn’t competing. He was there to support his older brother Umar, who was booked against Urijah Faber. Dvalishvili defeated Umar in a UFC title fight in January 2025 so there seems to be a grudge. Fighter Islam Makhachev says Dvalishvili had previously insulted the assailant’s mother. Everyone involved, including Dvalishvili and Lazishvili, remained detained. Real American Freestyle has barred Usman from attending Saturday’s event. The video lets everyone see who approached whom and how the confrontation began. Arresting people for recording that gives seems very Abu Dhabi. #6153. Not All Property Tax Cuts Are Created Equal

Fiscal conservatives’ aim should be the same as for other taxes: broaden the base, reduce the rate.

An aerial view of a suburban neighborhood in central Florida.

We can at least say this of last Tuesday: It was a great day for homeowners upset over their property taxes. Across five states, voters approved seven ballot measures to directly reduce or otherwise limit local taxes on different kinds of property. Conservatives, instinctively anti-tax in almost every instance, cheered these initiatives.

Yet nuance is needed. Given that taxation is the necessary price of government, conservatives have long accepted that some taxes are better than others. Likewise, some kinds of property taxes are preferable to others, and therefore, not all cuts to property taxes are created equal. Some may even be worse than the status quo.

John R. Puri is the Thomas L. Rhodes Fellow at National Review.

We can at least say this of last Tuesday: It was a great day for homeowners upset over their property taxes. Across five states, voters approved seven ballot measures to directly reduce or otherwise limit local taxes on different kinds of property. Conservatives, instinctively anti-tax in almost every instance, cheered these initiatives.

Yet nuance is needed. Given that taxation is the necessary price of government, conservatives have long accepted that some taxes are better than others. Likewise, some kinds of property taxes are preferable to others, and therefore, not all cuts to property taxes are created equal. Some may even be worse than the status quo.

Call it the ultimate Nile River cruise experience.

River cruise giant Viking has unveiled an epic new itinerary that sails the entire 600-mile stretch of the waterway between Cairo in the north and Aswan in the south.

Dubbed the Grand Nile Journey, Viking's 19-day trip revives a longer Nile cruise route that dates back to the late 1800s, when paddle steamers carried travelers from Cairo on the 465-mile journey south to Luxor, home to some of ancient Egypt's most famous temples and burial grounds.

From there, the vessels would continue to Aswan, another 130 miles to the south, with stops at ancient temples along the way.

Nowadays, most Nile River sailings skip the first 465 miles of this historic route, with ships only traveling along the 130-mile stretch of the Nile between Luxor and Aswan. Passengers reach the ships by flying from Cairo to Luxor, typically after a few days exploring Cairo.

Related: The ultimate guide to Nile river cruises and cruisetours

Only a handful of vessels currently operate a longer itinerary of the sort that Viking has announced — and none at the luxury level for which Viking is known on the river.

Kicking off in 2028 but available to book now, Viking's new Grand Nile Journeys will begin with a three-night stay at a luxury hotel in Cairo (the line often puts guests in the elegant Fairmont Nile City, along the banks of the river). Then, passengers board the line's one-of-a-kind, all-suite vessel Viking Ra for the 14-night journey south to Aswan.

The voyages will include stops at ancient sites along the 450-mile stretch from Cairo to Luxor that most Nile River travelers never see, including the 4,600-year-old Meidum Pyramid near Beni Suef and the striking cliffside Noble Tombs of Beni Hasan.

Other rare stops will include a visit to Tell el-Amarna, the once-lost royal desert capital founded by the Pharaoh Akhenaten, and the Abydos Temple, famous for drawings of ancient pilgrims to the sacred Festival of Osiris.

After a week traveling south along this lesser-visited stretch of the Nile, the Viking Ra will arrive in Luxor for another week of travel southward along the more popular parts of the river.

An extended stop in Luxor will bring visits to the temples of Luxor and Karnak, the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Seti I at Abydos.

Additional stops include the Temple of Horus in Edfu and the Temple of Philae near Aswan, among other sites in this area.

Related: The 5 best destinations you can visit on a Viking ship

By following this long route from Cairo to Aswan, the new Grand Nile Journeys will echo the long Nile sailing that Agatha Christie made famous in her 1937 novel "Death on the Nile." She wrote the book after taking one of the long journeys in 1933 on the Thomas Cook & Son luxury paddle steamer S.S. Sudan.

The first few days of each of the new Grand Nile Journeys in Cairo will include visits to the Great Pyramids of Giza, the Great Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum.

At the end of the trip, passengers will also spend a final night at a hotel in Cairo before departing.

Passengers can extend their trips with optional pre- and postcruise land tours that include an extra two-night stay in Cairo and a four-night, fully guided excursion to nearby Jordan for visits to the Dead Sea, Petra and Amman.

While dating back to the late 1800s, when Thomas Cook & Son introduced "rapid steamers" that sailed the Nile from Cairo to Aswan, such longer Nile itineraries continued to be common until 1994, when the Egyptian government officially closed the 465-mile stretch of the river between Cairo and Luxor to overnight passenger ships due to security worries. Low water levels and shifting sandbars in the river also played a role.

After nearly 20 years of closure, the Egyptian government reopened the Cairo-to-Luxor stretch of the river to cruise vessels in 2012, following extensive river dredging, irrigation upgrades and major security overhauls. But long sailings from Cairo to Aswan have been slow to rebound.

Among the handful of other companies offering such trips is Movenpick Hotels & Resorts, which markets 14-night sailings from Cairo to Aswan on the 52-cabin MS Darakum.

Former CIA station chief Dan Hoffman examines reported Iranian threats that prompted Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his family to relocate to a military base. He also discusses allegations of Iranian cyberattacks in France and reported cooperation between Iran and Russia to circumvent U.S. military and economic restrictions.

Attorney General Todd Blanche has been living at a military installation in the Washington, D.C., area for months, joining a growing roster of senior Trump administration officials residing in military housing, three sources familiar with the arrangement confirmed to Fox News Digital.

A source familiar with the arrangement did not elaborate on the reason for the move earlier this year. Fox News Digital reached out to the Department of Justice for comment.

Among the other top officials residing on military installations is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who recently relocated amid reported threats linked to Iran.

The living arrangements have placed senior civilian officials in housing traditionally associated with military leadership, amid security concerns ranging from reported threats tied to drug cartels to fears of Iranian retaliation.

US EVACUATES 13 MILITARY AIRCRAFT FROM SECOND UK BASE AS NEW IRAN THREAT RAISES ALARM

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche speaks during a news conference at the Department of Justice on April 7, 2026. (Getty Images)

Blanche’s predecessor, Pam Bondi, also quietly relocated from her Washington apartment to military housing after law enforcement flagged threats tied to drug cartels, The New York Times reported in March. The Times also cited threats related to backlash over her handling of the Epstein files, although the Justice Department disputed that explanation.

Iran has intensified efforts to target Americans, including current and former U.S. officials, as Bessent recently relocated to a military base amid threats linked to Tehran, a source familiar with the situation confirmed to Fox News Digital Wednesday.

"After The Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary’s Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase, which have now forced the secretary to relocate to a military base for his safety. The news media has an obligation to act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials," a different source familiar with the move told Fox News Digital Wednesday.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth have reportedly taken up residence at Fort McNair in Washington, D.C., while White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and other administration officials have moved to military installations or protected government housing.

SECRET SERVICE CHIEF SAYS THREATS AGAINST PROTECTEES UP 40%, CITES INTERNET AND MENTAL HEALTH

War Secretary Pete Hegseth, far left, and Vice President JD Vance, far right, laugh together during a ceremony on the South Lawn of the White House, April 28, 2026. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

The relocations have not all stemmed from the same threats. Some followed concerns about domestic political violence, while Bessent's move comes amid reported threats linked to Iran.

Fort McNair, a historic Army installation along the Potomac River in Washington, D.C., has emerged as one of the military properties housing senior Trump administration officials. The installation, which dates to the late 1700s, is home to the National Defense University and traditionally provides residential quarters for senior military leaders.

ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP

President Donald Trump attends a Cabinet meeting at the White House in Washington on May 27, 2026. (Jacquelyn Martin/AP)

Fort McNair's residential quarters are divided into two housing groups, according to a 2020 National Capital Planning Commission report, while a 2024 Army filing identifies 27 historic homes built before 1919 at the installation.

The Army's housing website lists 88 historic dwelling units across Fort McNair and nearby Fort Myer combined, without specifying how many are at each base.

Other officials previously reported to have used military housing include former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Army Secretary Daniel Driscoll. The arrangements have involved different installations.

Korean Air is adding a second New York-area gateway.

The SkyTeam Alliance carrier will land at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) with flights from Seoul’s Incheon Airport (ICN) in May 2027, Korean Air said on Thursday. The new route to east of the Hudson River complements its long-standing twice-daily service to New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).

Korean Air will offer daily flights to EWR from May 22. It will fly a Boeing 777-300ER on the route.

The airline did not say what 777 configuration it will fly to EWR. It flies planes with several layouts, including an older configuration with eight first class suites.

United Airlines launched its first-ever nonstop from EWR to ICN in September. The Star Alliance carrier flies a Boeing 787-9 on the route.

Korean Air’s new EWR flight comes at a time of change for the airline as it wraps up a merger with fellow Korean carrier Asiana. Korean will complete the customer-facing integration of Asiana on Dec. 17, a combination that will significantly increase its market share at ICN.

While the merger does not add any new U.S. destinations to Korean Air’s map, it does increase its presence at JFK to up to four daily flights including Asiana, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium shows.

First look: Inside Korean Air’s stunning new flagship lounge at LAX

Future schedules show Korean Air continuing to serve JFK with four daily flights through June 2027.

The new EWR flight will complement Korean Air’s JFK services and create a new connection with joint venture partner Delta Air Lines. The carriers have expanded their transpacific options in recent years with new routes, including Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) to ICN on Delta.

The partnership allows Delta and Korean Air to coordinate commercial matters, including fares and schedules, between the U.S. and South Korea.

Korean Air highlighted the expanded flight options and New Jersey’s pharmaceutical, biotechnology, financial, and logistics industrial clusters for its new EWR route.

EWR is Korean Air’s first new U.S. destinations since it added Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) in 2019.

#6148. The Rise of the Rosé States

A rosé state’s political disposition is recognizably Republican, but that disposition is conditional on a normie GOP.

Karno Muji Saputra/Getty Images, NR Illustration

When Ted Cruz was up for reelection in Texas in 2024 (and Trump hadn’t yet been swept back into power), I had a conversation with a political operative who had just gotten back from running a mock debate with him. We talked about Cruz and John Cornyn and what kind of Republican each was, and how they would fare in a world where Trump completed his comeback.

I spitballed an idea that had been kicking around in my head for a time: that Texas wasn’t as red as everybody thought, or at least not as uniformly MAGA; that it was still much closer to the state George W. Bush took over from outgoing Governor Ann Richards in 1995; and that election results had largely masked an underlying political disposition that was a quite light shade of red. Given that reality, I said, Cornyn was a better indication of where Texas voters were than Cruz.

Karno Muji Saputra/Getty Images, NR Illustration

#6147. Ken Paxton Spotted Fleeing Texas With Girlfriend After Voters Reject His Senate Bid—Flying Coach To Fiji

Eight days after losing his U.S. Senate race, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was photographed at San Francisco airport with his girlfriend, Tracy Duhon, wearing a straw hat and carrying a Republican Attorneys General Association backpack. They were apparently headed to Fiji. And photos show them in coach. They departed Wednesday night, November 11. A witness says they worried about their bags making it to Fiji. Michael Board shares the photo of Ken Paxton and Tracy Duhon at San Francisco airport Another photo shows them standing in the aisle of coach. TMZ: Ken Paxton spotted in San Francisco International Airport, witness says he was traveling to Fiji https://t.co/GNFXuDuPvY — Kalshi Politics (@KalshiPolitics) November 12, 2026 Meanwhile, Paxton’s divorce finalized Thursday. State Senator Angela Paxton filed to end their 38-year marriage last year “on biblical grounds.” I’ve covered the travels of Ted Cruz, Elizabeth Warren, AOC, Bernie Sanders and others, and the credit card spend habits of former Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker. This choice isn’t partisan. Paxton Has A History Of Getting Out Of Town A Texas politician fleeing the state for warmer climes brings to mind Ted Cruz flying to Cancún during the February 2021 winter storm while millions of Texans were without power. This time the disaster was electoral. But Paxton has his own winter storm escape story. He and his then-wife went to Utah during that same freeze, saying he had meetings with Utah’s attorney general about the state Google antitrust case. This summer, I wrote about Paxton spending America’s 250th birthday in London with Duhon. He marked the anniversary of separating from Britain by going to Britain. The pair had been spotted traveling through Washington Dulles on their way to Iceland in late June. Then came the London video, with Marriott County Hall in the background. They apparently flew economy on that trip. Video of Ken Paxton and Tracy Duhon in London over the Fourth of July weekend In October, the Wall Street Journal reported on video of Paxton and Duhon celebrating New Year’s Eve 2024 overlooking the Burj Khalifa fireworks with fugitives indicted in a federal healthcare fraud case who had contributed $190,000 to Paxton’s campaign. James Talarico’s campaign shares footage of Ken Paxton at the Dubai gathering Republicans Knew Who They Were Nominating The Republican-controlled Texas House impeached Attorney General Paxton. Paxton’s own senior staff reported him to the FBI. House investigators alleged that an Austin real estate developer provided home renovations and helped conceal Paxton’s activities, including through an Uber account under the name “Dave P.” He also employed a woman Paxton previously had an affair with. The Uber account apparently let Paxton carry on his affair and visit his donor without his security detail or using his identifiable state vehicle. In return, Paxton allegedly used his office to help the developer. One example was a rushed legal opinion invoking pandemic restrictions to stop foreclosure auctions. The Texas Senate, under pressure large donors and the Lieutenant Governor, acquitted him in 2023. He’d also spent years under state felony securities fraud charges. That case ended through an agreement requiring restitution, community service and ethics training. The federal corruption investigation ended without charges. President Trump endorsed Paxton against incumbent Senator John Cornyn a week before their May runoff. Republicans then had to spend heavily defending a seat they’d held for decades, with a candidate that may have been one of the worst campaigners I’ve seen in 30 years even apart from his past challenges. Here he is wearing a reported-$40,000 watch and a Four Seasons golf shirt. And this clip of him was promoted by his campaign: .@KenPaxtonTX: The future of our state and the future of our country ride on this race. https://t.co/2ZvVWdhwzp — Paxton War Room (@PaxtonsPatriots) August 29, 2026 That choice cost Republicans dearly. Cornyn would’ve been far better-positioned in the general election. Counterfactuals are hard, but the rest of his party’s nominees at the state level were clearly brought down by his place on the ticket. Republicans even appeared in advertising against him. Former Republican state Representative Glenn Rogers, who’d voted to impeach Paxton, appeared in a pro-Talarico ad saying he’d never trust or support Paxton. The most revealing ad may have been the one Angela Paxton made because polls showed over 10% of Republicans staying home. While divorcing him, she urged Republicans to vote without mentioning her husband by name: “It’s about getting the whole team across the finish line.” Paxton wasn’t the only Republican with problems. Governor Greg Abbott had helped defeat Republican legislators who opposed school choice in the 2024 primaries. That left resentment in rural communities where public schools are major employers, and there are fewer private school options where the vouchers could be used. Republicans also faced a terrible national election environment, with an unpopular President and high gas prices. I Even Agree With Him On Some Of His Lawsuits Just this morning, I wrote about Austin’s airport rail plans and the financing arrangement Paxton’s office challenged. The city raised property taxes, then routed the money through a separate corporation to issue the debt, allowing the city to claim that it isn’t borrowing. Economically, property taxes support the bonds, while the city claims its not running afoul on state borrowing rules. Expedia Group confirmed Thursday that attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider, in a supply chain cyberattack that also affected multiple companies.

Expedia Group confirmed Thursday that attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider, part of a supply chain attack that hit multiple companies. The acknowledgment followed reports on cybersecurity sites this week about claims by an extortion group known as n0n that it had stolen Expedia data. Expedia said it contained the issue as soon as it became aware, is investigating with outside security experts, and that its platforms remain safe for travelers and partners. The company did not identify the compromised vendor or say what information may have been exposed, and the scale of the breach is unconfirmed. Separately, researchers at Wiz and Sentra documented an attack between October 14 and 26 involving cloud data platform Qubole, a onetime Expedia vendor, in which attackers used compromised credentials to enter multiple customers' cloud environments and download data. Sentra found that former Qubole customers never revoked the access permissions they had previously granted, leaving a way in long after the business relationships ended. Expedia did not confirm whether its breach is related to Qubole, and outside researchers have not publicly identified Expedia as one of the affected customers.

#6144. One Night in Bangkok: Eurovision Asia Tests Thailand’s Bet on Events

Enter your email for a complimentary article + exclusive offers.

Photo Caption: Bangkok city night view with main traffic high way.

Thailand wants events to offset falling arrivals. Early data shows Eurovision Asia riding Bangkok's seasonal upswing, not driving it. One night won't move the needle, but a steady calendar of events just might.

Bangkok hosts the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia on Nov. 14, with 11 countries competing at One Bangkok Forum. It is an early test of Thailand's new tourism playbook: earn more from each visitor as arrivals stall.

"Hosting the first-ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia reflects Thailand's Value over Volume direction, where global events are leveraged to deliver quality tourism, meaningful experiences and long-term benefits for local communities," Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) Governor Thapanee Kiatphaibool said in April.

At least at first, the payoff is likely to be publicity rather than spending. "For this first edition, I expect visibility and discovery to be the main benefits," said Nat Srinara, a Singapore-based hospitality consultant and lecturer at EHL Hospitality Business School.

Thailand's draft tourism plan targets at least 4 trillion baht ($118 billion) in annual revenue by 2032, about 48% above 2025, Skift

Thailand hosts the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok on November 14, an early test of its "Value over Volume" tourism strategy as arrivals fall. Foreign visitors dropped 7.2% to 32.9 million in 2025, and the Tourism Authority of Thailand now expects just over 31 million this year, below the government's earlier 33 million forecast — yet the draft tourism plan targets at least 4 trillion baht ($118 billion) in annual revenue by 2032, roughly 48% above 2025, with no budget, arrivals assumption, or spending-per-visitor goal attached. TAT has published no revenue estimate for Eurovision Asia and told Skift it does not oversee the contest, in contrast with Tomorrowland's Pattaya edition in December, which TAT projects will generate about 5.3 billion baht ($158 million) and which carries a disclosed 2 billion baht ($60 million) state commitment over five years. The early data points in two directions: Agoda searches by Asian travelers for Bangkok stays over the contest window rose 14% year over year and Amadeus shows air arrivals up 11% for November 12 to 14, but hotel occupancy of 60% and ADR of $143.20 show similar gains before and after the contest, which Amadeus said suggests a broader trend rather than a festival-specific spike. Bangkok could use the help: third-quarter RevPAR fell 5.3% from the previous quarter, and Kasikorn Research Center counted 148 hotel and accommodation closures nationwide through September, up 42%.

#6143. “The sitting president doesn’t win”: Ahead of midterms, Trump reflects on himself

On the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”

“When you vote, remember a party that hates America cannot be allowed to rule over the people who built our country,” Trump said, referring to Democrats, whom he said want to “blow all of this up by electing communist jihadists.”

“If the people that voted for me and voted in the last election where we had such a great victory, if they go out and vote, just a good portion of them, we will win in a landslide,” Trump said midway in his speech. “Now that doesn’t happen because usually whoever the sitting president is, Republican or Democrat, uh, good or bad, good president, great president, bad, for some reason the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms, but we gave this a very strong shot.”

The last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the New York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

Meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the New York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how big a role early votes will play in the outcome.

#6142. Where Does the U.S.-Israel Relationship Go from Here?

Opposition to Israel now has a toehold in both parties.

Israeli and American flags are flown at the March for Israel rally on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., November 14, 2023.

In the days since the midterms, it has become clear that the U.S.-Israel relationship is under assault in both parties. On the left, a group of DSA-linked Democrats has been elected to Congress. Like their precursor Zohran Mamdani in New York City and led by Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, these new members place opposition to Israel at the center of their politics. It isn’t one concern among many but the defining issue of their candidacies. El-Sayed used his graceless and vengeful victory speech to attack Israel in barely disguised language: “Michiganders, we want our taxes spent here for schools here and health care here and infrastructure here. We don’t want our money sent to do apartheid or genocide or war.”

For the first time, both the Senate and the House will have — among the majority side — dedicated opponents of all aid to Israel, including even the sale of defensive weapons. They will see moves like an end to military assistance as weak half-measures, when much more must be demanded.

Israeli and American flags are flown at the March for Israel rally on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., November 14, 2023.

Cardmembers can access American Express Centurion Lounges, receive a Priority Pass Select membership (enrollment required) and visit Delta Sky Clubs when flying on eligible same-day Delta flights. Delta Sky Club access is limited to 10 visits per year unless you spend $75,000 on eligible purchases in a calendar year to unlock unlimited visits. Access is subject to eligibility requirements.

Amex also operates Centurion Lounges at more than 20 airports, so the benefit can be particularly valuable if you live near or frequently connect through an airport with one.

If you travel frequently and would otherwise pay for lounge access, the Platinum could help you save money while making your time at the airport more comfortable. And when combined with the card's other travel benefits and statement credits, lounge access can help make the $895 annual fee easier to justify.

While the is best known for its premium travel benefits, it also offers a growing list of lifestyle statement credits that can help offset its $895 annual fee.

For example, cardmembers can receive up to $400 in Resy statement credits each calendar year (distributed as up to $100 per quarter) at eligible U.S. Resy restaurants* and up to $300 in Lululemon statement credits* (up to $75 quarterly) at U.S. stores (excluding outlets) and online.

The card also offers up to $300 annually in digital entertainment statement credits* (up to $25 monthly) for eligible subscriptions, along with up to $120 annually toward an Uber One membership to fully cover an auto-renewing $96 annual or $9.99 monthly membership*.

If you're already spending money on dining, shopping and entertainment in these categories, the credits can provide meaningful value without requiring you to change your spending habits.

However, many of these benefits are divided into monthly or quarterly credits, so you'll need to keep track of when to use them. The Platinum is a particularly good fit for someone who doesn't mind managing these benefits and can consistently take advantage of them year-round.

Related: How to maximize benefits with the American Express Platinum

The Amex Platinum can also be a valuable addition to your wallet if you regularly stay at Hilton, Marriott or luxury hotels.

Cardmembers receive complimentary Hilton Honors Gold and Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite status, which can provide benefits such as bonus points on stays and potential room upgrades. You'll also receive Leaders Club Sterling status with The Leading Hotels of the World, a collection of independent luxury hotels. Enrollment is required for select benefits.

Beyond elite status, one of the Platinum's most valuable hotel-related perks is its up to $600 annual lodging statement credit (up to $300 semiannually).

Cardmembers can receive up to $300 in statement credits every six months on eligible prepaid bookings through American Express Travel®, including stays at Fine Hotels + Resorts and The Hotel Collection properties, as well as select Airbnb Luxe stays.

The Hotel Collection and Airbnb Luxe require a minimum two-night stay, and beginning Jan. 1, 2027, Fine Hotels + Resorts bookings will also require at least two nights to qualify for the lodging credit.

Fine Hotels + Resorts bookings also come with valuable benefits, including daily breakfast for two, guaranteed 4 p.m. late checkout, room upgrades when available and a property credit valued at $100.

If you regularly book these types of stays, the lodging credit and additional perks can go a long way toward offsetting the card's annual fee. Just be sure to compare prices with booking directly, since rates through Amex Travel aren't always the lowest.

Related: How to maximize the Amex Platinum hotel statement credit

Chase's unofficial 5/24 rule generally makes applicants ineligible for many Chase cards if they've opened five or more personal credit cards across issuers within the past 24 months.

Travelers who are still eligible for Chase cards may want to prioritize products such as the (see rates and fees) or (see rates and fees) before exceeding that threshold.

If you've already built a collection of Chase rewards cards, the Amex Platinum could be worth considering as your next premium travel card.

The card also earns Membership Rewards points, giving you access to a separate collection of airline and hotel transfer partners that can complement an existing Chase Ultimate Rewards strategy.

Many people just starting in the points world underestimate the stringency of Chase’s 5/24 rule. If you're just getting started with travel rewards and remain under Chase's 5/24 threshold, you may want to think carefully before applying for the Amex Platinum.

Opening the card could count toward your 5/24 total and potentially limit your eligibility for Chase cards in the future. That could mean missing out on valuable welcome offers or benefits from cards you planned to open later.

However, once you get over 5/24, it may be hard to get back under, and there’s a massive opportunity cost in doing so. Having a plan and sticking to it will serve you well in the long term.

Of course, that doesn't mean everyone under 5/24 should avoid the Platinum. If its benefits are a particularly good fit for your travel habits, it may still make sense.

The provides 5 Membership Rewards points per dollar spent on flights booked directly with airlines or with American Express Travel (on up to $500,000 of spending each calendar year, then 1 point per dollar spent).

A card like the or (see rates and fees) may be a better fit because their broader travel earning categories can include eligible third-party airfare bookings.

The offers a long list of statement credits, but that doesn't necessarily mean every cardholder will get enough value from them to justify the $895 annual fee.

Following the card's 2025 refresh, several of its benefits are geared toward specific lifestyle purchases, including dining at Resy restaurants, shopping at Lululemon and purchasing an Oura Ring. (Cardmembers receive up to a $200 Oura Ring statement credit each calendar year. This statement credit applies to ring purchases only and doesn't cover subscriptions. Enrollment is required.)

Many of these credits also come with restrictions. For example, the Resy and Lululemon credits are distributed quarterly, meaning you'll need to use them throughout the year rather than all at once.

If you don't already spend money with these merchants, or you don't want to keep track of multiple credits and enrollment requirements, the Platinum may not be the best fit.

Before applying, carefully consider just how much these credits are worth to you; if they provide little to no value, another Amex card might be a better fit.

Related: 4 different flavors of Amex Platinum — which one is right for you?

Business owners with substantial expenses may find that is a better fit than the personal Platinum.

Although both cards carry an $895 annual fee (see rates and fees), their earning rates and statement credits differ in ways that could make one more valuable than the other.

For example, the Business Platinum earns 2 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases in select business categories and on purchases of $5,000 or more, on up to $2 million in combined eligible purchases per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar.

The Business Platinum also provides up to $1,150 in statement credits per calendar year for U.S. Dell purchases: up to $150 each calendar year and an additional $1,000 statement credit after spending $5,000 on Dell purchases with the same card each calendar year (enrollment required).

You can also access the Pay with Points redemption option on the Business Platinum card, which gets you a 35% bonus for eligible flights with your selected airline using your Amex points (up to 1 million points back per calendar year). This is notably not available on the personal Amex Platinum.

These business-focused benefits may be more useful for someone with significant company expenses, while the personal Platinum may be a better fit for travelers who can maximize its lifestyle credits.

New cardmembers can find out their offer and may be eligible for as high as 175,000 bonus points after spending $12,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. (Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.)

Based on TPG's November 2026 valuations, that bonus could be worth up to $3,500, which is nearly four times the card's $895 annual fee.

While this is the card's standard welcome offer, now could still be a good time to apply if you're eligible for an offer you're happy with and can comfortably meet the spending requirement without making unnecessary purchases.

Just make sure you'll also get enough value from the card's ongoing benefits to justify its annual fee beyond the first year.

Related: The best time to apply for Amex cards based on offer history

The offers an impressive lineup of premium travel benefits and statement credits, but its $895 annual fee means it won't make sense for everyone.

For frequent travelers who value airport lounge access and luxury hotel perks, and can consistently use the card's lifestyle credits, there's plenty of potential to get more value than the annual fee.

On the other hand, travelers who prefer straightforward rewards or don't regularly use the card's benefits may find better value with a lower-annual-fee option.

Ultimately, the Platinum is worth considering if its benefits fit your existing spending and travel habits — not because of the total advertised value of its credits.

To learn more, check out our full review of the Amex Platinum.

#6139. Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

Showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses. “Who Is America?” The answer, on its face, will not surprise you: we are a nation of easy marks. Not merely easy, but willing.

Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.

Back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom. But today, being on camera is so natural and desirable to most of us that we are willing to say or do just about anything for a few of the 15 minutes we believe to be our birthright.

“Ali G” and the characters the show introduced, including Borat Sagdiyev and Brüno Gehard, also were born years before Project Veritas and InfoWars and other right-wing vehicles of disinformation made hidden camera hoaxing into something sinister.

All of which is to say, “Who Is America?” is not, as Showtime would like you to believe, “the most dangerous show in history.” At best, it is an occasionally funny one.

But to anyone who mourns the collective deterioration of our population’s capacity to engage in critical thought, but has no idea of how urgent of a crisis that happens to be, Baron Cohen’s new endeavor is less of a comedy than a fright show. “Who Is America?” A nation of pliable dullards ripe for the hacking.

“Who Is America?” was produced in secret, and its pre-show marketing largely consisted of publicized declarations of outrage by such right-wing figures as Joe Walsh, Sarah Palin and Roy Moore. Each attempted to transform their extreme embarrassment at having been duped by a British clown hiding behind layers of latex and spirit gum into some approximation of righteous anger at said comedian’s dishonesty.

Showtime, meanwhile, maintained the aura of mystery surrounding the series almost to the brink of its debut, revealing the title only a little more than a week prior. The network released the briefest of clips featuring one famous interview subject, Dick Cheney.

This in itself was a bit of flimflam Showtime’s part: “Hope you’ll tune in next week for an interview with me,” Cheney says in the video, only to be a no-show in the premiere.

You can’t blame “Who Is America?” for saving its biggest fish for later, because the famous politicians in the opener prove the problem of our collective gullibility just fine by themselves. In fact, although liberals may have gotten a hearty guffaw out of hearing Palin’s wailing about having been faked out by Baron Cohen, the very same character — Dr. Billy Wayne Ruddick Jr. PhD of Truthbrary.org — sat down for a conversation with none other than the honorable junior senator from Vermont, Bernie Sanders.

Prior to the premiere Billy Wayne tweeted a response to Palin’s accusation that he made fun disabled veterans. “I did NOT say I was a War Vet,” Ruddick’s “official” response reads, going on to explain that the service was in was “not military, but United Parcel”.

Nor does he make such assertions to Sanders, with whom he debates the merits of a universal healthcare plan. And when I say debate, what I mean is that Sanders very calmly shares statistics with Billy Wayne long after the interviewer’s line of questioning stops making sense. And when Sanders asks Billy Wayne to confirm that he is disabled, given that he is conducting the interview while seated on a motorized scooter, Baron Cohen’s character replies that no, he is not. “This here scooter is to preserve my body’s finite energy,” Billy Wayne says.

READ MORE: That viral “strangers on a plane” Twitter story: Not a rom-com but a horror show

One may be tempted to qualify Sanders’ appearance by pointing out that he acquitted himself well in the face of a person best be described as a few coconuts short of a beach vacation in Binomo.

But this fails to answer the question of why Sanders signed a release, allowing this interview to be broadcast. Did anyone on Sanders’ team vet Truthbrary.org the moment Billy Wayne mentioned it? Even if they thought he was genuine, what is to be gained from being seen in a televised debate with a guy whose site includes a page titled  “Obamanoids — For Real!”?

(To be fair, reportedly Baron Cohen almost fooled veteran news anchor Ted Koppel as part of his project. Koppel told The Hollywood Reporter that he was contacted to appear in a Showtime project titled “Age of Reason,” said to feature “conversations with distinguished experts in science and public policy, highlighting the brightest and most reputable minds on today’s most important topics.” Koppel, perhaps receiving brainwaves from his colleague Sam Donaldson, wised up before Baron Cohen could pull him too deeply into his game.)

A second character introduced in the premiere, an NPR shirt-wearing hyper-liberal named  Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, visits the opulent South Carolina home of wealthy Trump supporters he says are  “afflicted with white privilege.” But it soon becomes clear that his marks’ problem isn’t close-mindedness but over-correcting in the acceptance department. When Baron Cohen’s interviewer waxes on about encouraging his daughter Malala to “free bleed” on the American flag as a lesson, they simply nod and listen; when he chats about his wife’s ongoing affair with a dolphin, they don’t have any questions like, say, whether what they’re hearing is real.

This brings us to another answer to “Who Is America?”: we’re so aware of cameras, and desperate to have its focus upon us, that we will do and say anything without thinking of its possible permanence.

Demonstrating this is Baron Cohen’s third character Rick Sherman, an ex-con turned TV host who visits a Laguna Beach, California gallery to show his work, which is a series of capable but otherwise unextraordinary portraits rendered in feces and ejaculate.

Now, it’s entirely possible that the woman who runs the gallery might have been thinking she could have the next Andres Serrano on her hands. On the other hand, please.

This is a subject entirely aware of being on view, so obsessed with appearing erudite that while Rick is off camera, having excused himself to the facilities to commit another brown-and-white vision to paper, she addresses the camera like the host she was born to be.

“Who knew the world was capable of such oxymoronic paradoxical juxtapositions?” she muses. And this is before the homemade pubic hair paintbrush comes out.

Baron Cohen has pushed the limits of tolerant everyday people many times in the past, mostly in a way that makes them look reasonable or, at the very least, more intelligent than the put-ons he inflicts upon them. And this is perhaps one of the most depressing aspects about “Who Is America?”, its demonstration of how endemic our lack of analysis truly is. I’m not saying that gallery owner is a stupid woman, understand.

But her interview is an example of prizing exposure over lasting consequence. By that I’m not merely referring to the fact that she placated a man who not only handed her pieces of cardboard purportedly smeared with his own dried excrement, or waited to receive a fresh sample of his work, but that she decided she needed to share her expert observation as to why she needed to do so by uttering a sentence full of five dollar words that add up to absolute nonsense.

(Either that or she’s a friend of Baron Cohen’s and in on the gag. I hope it’s option two, as opposed to her actually legitimizing the artistic relevance of number two.)

A number of reviews of “Who Is America?” have pointed out that Baron Cohen’s sneaky deceit is no longer funny because the formerly insane viewpoints Baron Cohen’s tactics expose have been normalized.

This has always been the danger, but it’s one every sort of parody or satire contends with in the current climate. It’s difficult to lampoon leaders seeking to legislate ludicrous patches to crises like gun violence instead of adopting common sense solutions like stricter regulation.

Which brings us to the portion of “Who Is America?” guaranteed to dominate Monday’s gallery of crazy clips, fronted by Baron Cohen’s Col. Erran Morad, a self-styled Israeli anti-terrorism expert who calls himself “the terrorist terminator.”

The fake Mossad officer is there to promote his “Kinderguardians” program, a proposal that aims to train and arm toddlers in the classroom because, Moran says, arming teachers is crazy.

And this is the portion that has Walsh’s boxers in a bunch, because he joins House representatives Dana Rohrabacher and Joe Wilson in lending on-camera endorsements. Walsh’s comments are interwoven with a series of fake testimonials from the likes of Larry Pratt, executive director emeritus of the lobbying group Gun Owners of America and rape joke enthusiast.

Nobody forced Walsh to say, with gusto, “The way to stop a bad guy with is a good child with a gun. Happy shooting, kids!” If he didn’t want to say it, he wouldn’t have.

What Walsh might be upset about is being upstaged by Pratt, who earns some of the episode’s biggest laughs by reading the “science” behind the effectiveness of the fake program, revealing he doesn’t know the difference between human anatomy and hitmakers who grace Billboard’s pop charts.

Yes, “Who Is America?” gets mileage out of highlighting the callousness, sexism and extraordinary gullibility of conservatives, as Baron Cohen always has. But the things they say to him in disguise aren’t all that different than what they’d say on CNN, Fox, MSNBC or talk radio. Whatever power his comedy used to reveal is diminished by the fact that the charlatans no longer operate in secret.

Next week’s episode introduces one or two new characters, although I don’t imagine they do anything more “dangerous” than the four we met on Sunday. For a number of viewers who love Baron Cohen’s schtick, that won’t matter.

To them “Who Is America?” is precisely on brand, showing Americans famous and everyday reacting to bizarre situations with varying degrees of what we consider to be normalcy in a time where the baseline version of normal is constantly morphing and shifting.

To other viewers, however, “Who Is America?” is a confirmation that Baron Cohen has run some tests and can confirm there is limited and ever decreasing brain activity in this worsening patient we know as America. It is something to behold, that’s for sure. But I’m not sure it’s the stuff of groundbreaking comedy. It’s not even really news.

#6138. AOC taps power player who helped Bernie Sanders defy the odds as major 2028 decision looms

A fierce leadership battle erupts within the Democratic Party following the midterms as progressives push for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to consider a 2028 presidential run. Joe Concha, a Fox News contributor, joins 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss the deep party division, progressive strategy, potential leadership shifts and more.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is tapping a key player behind Bernie Sanders' presidential fundraising operation as speculation swirls over whether the left-wing Democrat could launch her own White House bid in 2028.

Ocasio-Cortez split with her longtime digital fundraising firm, Middle Seat, Axios reported Thursday, citing three sources familiar with the matter. She has now tapped Aisle 518 Strategies, the firm led by Democratic strategist Tim Tagaris, who helped drive Sanders' record-breaking online fundraising operations during his 2016 and 2020 presidential campaigns, according to Axios.

The move comes as some progressive groups are calling for Ocasio-Cortez to jump into the White House race in 2028. There has also been mounting speculation that she could seek the Senate seat held by Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., in 2028, potentially setting up a Democratic primary showdown if Schumer seeks re-election.

AOC CAMPAIGN MEMO FRAMES GROWTH FROM PROGRESSIVE FIREBRAND TO NATIONAL DEMOCRATIC PARTY FORCE

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has emerged as a leading figure on the left and a potential contender in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential conversation. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

Ocasio-Cortez's office declined to comment to Fox News Digital on Thursday.

Middle Seat and Aisle 518 Strategies each did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests seeking comment.

Sanders' 2016 fundraising operation capitalized on major campaign moments and attacks from establishment Democrats to generate surges in small-dollar donations, helping propel the relatively obscure Vermont senator into an unexpectedly competitive primary battle against Hillary Clinton, Politico reported at the time.

"Internet fundraising is about taking potential energy and converting it into kinetic energy, and nobody has done that better than Bernie Sanders," veteran Democratic operative Ari Rabin-Havt told Politico back in 2016. "Tim [Tagaris] and his team are maximizing that. Their emails are superior."

Sanders' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Sanders' campaign raised $34.5 million in the final three months of 2019, according to the AP. He went on to briefly emerge as the Democratic front-runner in early 2020 before Joe Biden consolidated support and secured the nomination.

Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a Democrat from New York, departs following a vote at the US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. (Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

AOC OPENS UP ABOUT RACE, GENDER IN WEIGHING POSSIBLE 2028 WHITE HOUSE BID

Ocasio-Cortez previously parted ways with her longtime campaign manager and creative director earlier in 2026, and also recruited a few former aides, according to Axios.

"I know there is a lot of speculation about what I will decide to do in 2028," Ocasio-Cortez said in a recent fundraising email. "I get asked about it nearly every interview and event."

Still, Ocasio-Cortez told The Washington Sun in an interview published Wednesday that she plans to deliberate privately about her political future.

U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, D-N.Y., speaks during a rally on March 21, 2025, at Civic Center Park in Denver, Colo. (Chet Strange/Getty Images)

"I probably will not be sharing anything publicly for a little while," she told The Sun.
